claims.text: Every load-bearing artifact describes one and the same trip, so the identity limb of POL-RD-08 is met: TRP-00515 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare ledger, and the times line up — requested 17:30:00, accepted 17:30:40, arrived 17:35:40, started 17:36:40, GPS first fix 17:36:40, ended 18:37:40.

The governing distance for the threshold test is the trace figure, not the rounded copy on the trip record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 48.82 km against a booked optimal of 34.2 km, an excess of 14.62 km, which is 42.75% of optimal — past the 20% gate — and 14.62 km is far past the 0.8 km absolute gate. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The same 14.62 km excess is greater than the 8.0 km absolute materiality figure, so this is not merely an established deviation but a MATERIAL one — it is roughly eight times the amount an ordinary lane change or a forced U-turn could produce — and the driver_profile check mandated by POL-RD-06 is engaged.

The POL-RD-06 pattern test is satisfied on its first limb alone: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, which is '3 or more'. I do not rely on the near-synonym prior_deviation_flags = 5, which is a LIFETIME counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure this clause names, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting it.

Because the deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence — the 14.62 km trace excess, two gantries charged off the optimal corridor, and the driver's own admission that he missed the KPE split — POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of the charged total of SGD 62.28 in place of the POL-RD-02 partial, with the government/third-party ERP lines settled under POL-RD-09 rather than uplifted.

For the side-by-side comparison POL-RD-06(b) requires, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic on this METERED fare is: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 34.2 + 0.28 x 40.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 on-optimal-route ERP = SGD 41.45, so the partial refund is 62.28 - 41.45 = SGD 20.83, rounded up to the payable SGD 20.85. The uplifted figure of SGD 62.28 is where the rider should land.

The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-refund route on this trip: the rider was billed for distance and time actually driven, and POL-RD-02 runs as written.

The off-route ERP is refundable but must not be double-counted: both charged gantries — TPE (Seletar Link towards Punggol) and TPE (Punggol Rd towards Tampines), SGD 2.00 each, SGD 4.00 in total — carry on_optimal_route = false, and under POL-RD-09(1) off-route ERP is already comprehended in the refund and is itemised for transparency only, never added on top of the POL-RD-02 or POL-RD-06 figure.

The deviation is independently corroborated beyond the trace itself: the two charged gantries place the vehicle on the TPE corridor the booked optimal route does not use, and the driver's own filed statement concedes he 'missed [the KPE split] once'. I deliberately do not offer the billed distance as corroboration, because on this platform the meter is derived from the same trace and is not an independent source.

There is no gap problem here to push this case toward escalation: the trace covers 100% of the trip at a 10-second cadence, its gaps array is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and POL-RD-10(3) is not triggered. Even if it were, the off-optimal ERP gantries and the driver's admission would carry the claim under POL-RD-07(ii).

No exculpatory clause is available to the driver on this record. The only traffic advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00515-01, is MISSING — no payload, admissibility weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so there is no advisory naming any road segment the optimal route traverses, and POL-RD-03 cannot be run. The absence itself is citable.

Nor can POL-RD-04 excuse a metre of this route. The chat log holds a single message, sent by the rider at 17:48:40, which asks the driver to put the phone down; it names no place and no road, and its waypoint_hint is null, so on POL-RD-04's own terms the corroboration test is undecidable, the clause is unavailable, and the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 do not help the driver either: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, so there is no relocated endpoint to re-quote against, and vehicle_type is RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 does not apply and 34.2 km is the correct baseline.

Once the rider has shown identity and an over-threshold excess from an unimpaired trace, POL-RD-08 shifts the burden to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause — POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12. He points to none: his statement that the extra distance 'wasn't that much' cites no evidence ID at all, and on POL-RD-08 an assertion citing no evidence carries no weight.

POL-RD-06(c) additionally requires a referral to driver-conduct review on this material deviation, and the record supports it: the rider's in-app message at 17:48:40 — 'can you please put the phone down and drive', read at 17:49:05 — is on file, and the driver's own statement admits he was checking navigation on his phone. That referral is an addition to the money, not a substitute for it.

The rider's own profile adds no extra burden: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the additional-corroboration rule in POL-RD-08 is not engaged, and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires — the trip identifiers match across all three artifacts, no timestamps disagree or run backwards, and every fare line has a counterpart in the trace or trip record.

This dispute was filed by the rider, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the present state leaves the rider carrying the whole SGD 62.28. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION would preserve exactly that charge, which is why nothing short of the refund is a rider win here, and FULL_REFUND of the contested amount is the outcome this evidence supports.

claims.text: The refund on this trip is arithmetic, not discretionary. On the booked optimal route the POL-RD-02 recomputation is ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 34.2 km + 0.28 x 40.0 min) x surge 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 40.65 + 0.80 = SGD 41.45, so the refund is charged_total 62.28 less 41.45 = SGD 20.83, rounded up to SGD 20.85. That figure — not the SGD 62.28 the rider seeks — is the whole of the rider's distance-and-time recovery.

The two off-route ERP gantry lines (SGD 2.00 each, SGD 4.00 in total, both recorded on_optimal_route false) are already comprehended inside that SGD 20.85, because the recomputed fare credits only gantries lying on the optimal route and the optimal-route ERP is SGD 0.00. Under POL-RD-09(1) those charges are itemised for transparency but must never be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, so the rider's total recovery cannot exceed SGD 20.85.

The full-refund gate in POL-RD-02 is nowhere near met: SGD 20.83 is 33.4% of the SGD 62.28 charged, far below the 90% share that would convert a partial refund into a full one. The rider's request for the entire contested amount fails on this arithmetic alone.

Both ERP charges are real crossings rather than phantom lines: the trace's nearest fix to the TPE (Seletar Link towards Punggol) gantry and to the TPE (Punggol Rd towards Tampines) gantry is 0.0 m for each. There is accordingly no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4) and no basis for a billing-integrity referral; the driver's route, however long, was actually driven and its charges are genuine.

The rider's conduct narrative does not move the money. POL-RD-02 makes the refund a computation from the fare_breakdown lines, and neither the single chat message (which carries waypoint_hint null and identifies no place or road) nor the rider's recollection alters a single line item; the rider's own timeline is overstated, since the trip ran 61 minutes, not the 90 asserted.

Honest concession, so that the dispute is confined to quantum: no exculpatory clause is available to the driver on this record. No traffic advisory is on file — EV-ADVIS-00515-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run; and the sole chat message carries waypoint_hint null and names no road, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test is undecidable on the record and that clause is unavailable. The driver therefore does not contest that the POL-RD-01 threshold is crossed, and advances no adjustment to the optimal route.

So far as the deviation is material and POL-RD-06 is consulted, limb (b) of that clause expressly does not uplift government-set and third-party pass-through lines, and all SGD 4.00 of ERP here is off-route pass-through settled under POL-RD-09. Any uplift under POL-RD-06(b) must therefore leave the SGD 4.00 of off-route ERP to the POL-RD-09 treatment and must state the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 20.85 side by side with the uplifted figure.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This is one trip, TRP-00515, and it is decided on clean evidence. The GPS trace covers 100% of the trip at a 10-second cadence, with no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0) and no jumps, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and nothing on it is discounted. On that trace the car covered 48.82 km against the booked optimal of 34.2 km — an excess of 14.62 km, which is 42.75% of optimal and clears both POL-RD-01 gates (20% and 0.8 km). The excess also exceeds the 8.0 km absolute figure, so the deviation is MATERIAL. The trip record's 48.8 km figure is a rounded copy and was not used for the threshold test.

The refund arithmetic, run as POL-RD-02 requires on this METERED fare, is: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 × 34.2 km + 0.28 × 40.0 min) × surge 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 on-optimal-route ERP = 41.45. Against charged_total of 62.28 that is 20.83, rounded up to a payable 20.85. That is the figure the driver's advocate put forward, and it is right as far as it goes — but only as the POL-RD-02 partial.

POL-RD-06 does more here. The deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence (the 14.62 km trace excess, the two off-optimal ERP gantries, and the driver's own filed admission that he missed the KPE split). The driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d = 3, which meets POL-RD-06's pattern test ('3 or more'), so the pattern is established and limb (b) applies. That limb licenses FULL_REFUND of the charged total in place of the POL-RD-02 partial. The two figures side by side, as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 figure 20.85; uplifted figure 62.28. The rider recovers 62.28.

The 4.00 of ERP (two TPE gantries at 2.00 each, both recorded on_optimal_route = false) is government/third-party pass-through, settled under POL-RD-09 and not uplifted. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the refund and is never added on top; both gantries were genuinely crossed (nearest trace fix 0.0 m to each), so there is no phantom line and no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4). The ERP portion is refunded at face value within the total, not doubled.

No exculpatory clause rescues the driver. The only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00515-01, is MISSING — no payload, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the driver does not contest that. The single chat message carries waypoint_hint null and names no place or road, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test is undecidable and the clause is unavailable. No endpoint was amended, so POL-RD-05 has nothing to re-quote, and the vehicle is RYDE_PLUS, not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and 34.2 km is the correct baseline. The driver's assertion that the extra distance 'wasn't that much' cites no evidence and carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The missing advisory is not relied on by this ruling, so it does not cap confidence (POL-GEN-02(2)).

On the rider's account: the elapsed time was 61 minutes, not the 90 asserted, so that part of the narrative is overstated, and the money does not turn on the phone-use allegations — but the deviation finding rests on the trace, not on the narrative. POL-RD-06(c) requires a referral to driver-conduct review, and that referral is recorded above; it is an addition to the money, not a substitute for it. Confidence is 0.9, consistent with the deciding artifacts (trace, fare ledger, trip record, driver profile) all carrying full weight 1.0.
referrals: POL-RD-06(c): refer the driver to driver-conduct review — a MATERIAL, substantiated deviation on trip TRP-00515 combined with an established repeat-deviation pattern (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 3) requires conduct review, and this referral rides with the monetary ruling without delaying it.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), the trip identifiers match across all three artifacts, no timestamps disagree or run backwards, no fare line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record, and the refund does not exceed the charged total. Under POL-RD-09(1) those charges are itemised for transparency but must never be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, so the rider's total recovery cannot exceed SGD 20.85.

The full-refund gate in POL-RD-02 is nowhere near met: SGD 20.83 is 33.4% of the SGD 62.28 charged, far below the 90% share that would convert a partial refund into a full one. The rider's request for the entire contested amount fails on this arithmetic alone.

Both ERP charges are real crossings rather than phantom lines: the trace's nearest fix to the TPE (Seletar Link towards Punggol) gantry and to the TPE (Punggol Rd towards Tampines) gantry is 0.0 m for each. There is accordingly no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4) and no basis for a billing-integrity referral; the driver's route, however long, was actually driven and its charges are genuine.

The rider's conduct narrative does not move the money. POL-RD-02 makes the refund a computation from the fare_breakdown lines, and neither the single chat message (which carries waypoint_hint null and identifies no place or road) nor the rider's recollection alters a single line item; the rider's own timeline is overstated, since the trip ran 61 minutes, not the 90 asserted.

Honest concession, so that the dispute is confined to quantum: no exculpatory clause is available to the driver on this record. No traffic advisory is on file — EV-ADVIS-00515-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run; and the sole chat message carries waypoint_hint null and names no road, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test is undecidable on the record and that clause is unavailable. The driver therefore does not contest that the POL-RD-01 threshold is crossed, and advances no adjustment to the optimal route.

So far as the deviation is material and POL-RD-06 is consulted, limb (b) of that clause expressly does not uplift government-set and third-party pass-through lines, and all SGD 4.00 of ERP here is off-route pass-through settled under POL-RD-09. Any uplift under POL-RD-06(b) must therefore leave the SGD 4.00 of off-route ERP to the POL-RD-09 treatment and must state the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 20.85 side by side with the uplifted figure.
